replyExamples.text: even after a 3-34 final, falcons still the only nfc south team that makes me nervous on purpose
I don’t buy the nostalgia. Data didn’t ruin football; pretending it tells the whole story did.
I’m ranking this above another generic superhero score sight unseen. Logan needs actual menace.
I’m not convinced Uncle Andrew needed this much mad-scientist energy, but Craig is selling it.
I don’t buy owners steering a musician’s tour. Buy a team, not the setlist.
No. 2 for Kawhi in both cities is generous. Duncan owns San Antonio; Lowry has the Toronto case.
Does the sequel need a fresh hook beyond the alternate-ending continuity, or is Will Smith enough to carry it?
Is “day to day” the optimistic label, or do you expect the Chargers matchup to be a real test?
Should public campaigning count against a player, or should the Ballon d’Or be judged strictly on the pitch?
Would you renew him before the deal is on paper, or is this Barcelona’s annual optimism?
Is this the new market floor for guards after one breakout season, or an overpay the Jazz will regret?
Is the chemistry doing more work than the tactics here?
Should the award follow the best season, or the biggest club?
Does a station owe listeners neutrality, or is choosing a side part of the job now?
Can a great cast sell a game before anyone knows the gameplay loop?
Is “not serious” now just code for “wait for Friday”?
Is Detroit–Buffalo actually the best game here, or is Sunday the one everyone circles?
Does Tyson’s old footage already say everything, or can this series still surprise people?
Does a prestige actor make the villain better, or just the trailer louder?
I don’t buy the “epic conclusion” copy. The truck-headlight shot sells this better than the tagline.
I don’t buy the clean binary here. The threat can be real and the politics opportunistic. What evidence would move you from “panic” to policy?
The repeatable signal is shared emotion turning a result into a community asset. Which matters more for that bond: the big nights or the week-to-week rituals?
I don’t buy “the right values” as a strategy until the delivery mechanism is named. For AI, defence and trade, which joint project gets the first proof point?
I don’t buy the equivalence. Is the right standard whether a public figure is mocked, or whether synthetic media is clearly labeled before it spreads?
The useful test isn’t “cheapest API”; it’s whether switching costs stay low when a team has to ship. Which metric should builders benchmark first: output consistency, latency or migration friction?

experiments.title: Voice/form shift — questions & disagreement vs observational one-liners
experiments.status: Closed — Testing / confidence weakened (2nd age done)
experiments.hypothesis: ≥50% questions/disagreements among next 30 replies raises engagement events and/or median views vs prior observational default.
experiments.change: Mix rules + AI-cadence ban; busy-room gate retained; ~8–15/day.
experiments.measurement: Mix tally each pass; median views; likes+replies+follows; follower delta vs prior 30.
experiments.result: 30/30 mix + 2nd age 2026-09-23: Q median 18 (n=20) / D 14.5 (n=10). Engagement ~2 events. Gap vs first age unchanged in substance.
experiments.conclusion: Form mix executable; Q>D slight and not actionable; engagement hypothesis unsupported on this sample.
experiments.decision: Hold EXP-03. Keep ops (busy-room + Q/D bias + go-hard). No Confirmed.

experiments.title: Busy-thread replies vs originals (public views)
experiments.hypothesis: For the week of Sep 8, the median public view count on selective replies into already-busy threads will be at least 2× the median public view count on that week’s originals.
experiments.change: Keep replies only where we have something real to say, preferring busy genuine rooms; keep at most one original per weekday for range (not a reply farm).
experiments.measurement: Each weekday after the pass, record public view counts (and any likes/replies/reposts/bookmarks) on that day’s original (if any) and each reply; also note follower count. Profile visits omitted (unknown without Premium).
experiments.result: Aged Sep 8–11 public views: selective replies n=18 median 19.5; originals n=4 median 10; ratio 1.95× (needed ≥2.0×; threshold 20). Top replies 1,377 / 799 / 628 still prove busy-room pattern; Fri quieter replies pulled median under bar.
experiments.conclusion: Busy-room quality beats reply count for a near-zero-follower account. Keep volume bar but gate on genuine busy openings; originals remain optional range.
experiments.decision: Sat 2026-09-12 morning closeout (metrics only — Sep 12 is Saturday). If median busy-thread reply views ≥2× median original views for Sep 8–11 aged posts, keep busy-thread bias under the new volume bar. If not, reopen where we spend attention.

lessons.experience: Recent replies followed EXP-02 form tallies but still read mechanical/AI to Thomas.

lessons.experience: Near-zero likes/follows persisted after EXP-01 and continued observational busy-room replies.
lessons.evidence: EXP-02 aged 2026-09-21: Q median 17 (n=19) vs D 13.5 (n=10); ~2 engagement events; followers 0.
lessons.learning: Impression-winning rooms + unchanged observational voice is insufficient — voice/form must change and be measured.
lessons.change: Keep busy-room + Q/D bias; add Thomas human-voice rules Tue onward (no binary-Q default, no stock D openers, parent-concrete, one clause, allow mess). Hold EXP-03 for 2nd age Wed.

lessons.experience: Across Sep 8–11, selective replies into already-busy rooms reached hundreds/thousands of views while standalone originals stayed in the low teens; expanding reply volume into quieter threads on Fri diluted the reply median to 19.5 vs originals’ 10.
lessons.evidence: Same @elephantharbor account, public view counts only (no Premium), full aged sample n=18 replies / n=4 originals. Ratio 1.95× vs ≥2.0× hypothesis. First follower appeared; Melbourne reply earned 2 likes.
lessons.learning: Busy-room quality beats reply count for a near-zero-follower account. Volume without busy-room bias can fail a median test even when the high end still proves the pattern.
lessons.change: Keep the ~8–15 weekday bar, but gate volume on genuine busy-thread openings; treat originals as range, not the growth lever. Do not chase quiet-room quota fills.

lessons.experience: Raised reply volume into mixed rooms while aged busy-thread replies (Zelda 1.3K, Schefter 627) still dwarf quiet originals (Venus 6, chess 2, jellyfish 8).
lessons.evidence: Same @elephantharbor account, public view counts, Sep 8–11 sample.
lessons.learning: Higher reply volume is compatible with the busy-room bias; originals remain optional range, not the growth lever, for a zero-follower account.
lessons.change: Keep shipping toward ~8–15 replies with busy-room preference; keep originals as range, not the main bet, through EXP-01 closeout.

lessons.experience: Sep 8–9 overnight, the Zelda remake reply reached 1,374 views and the Schefter Super Bowl LXI reply 615, while the Venus original stayed at 3 and the jellyfish original at 7.
lessons.evidence: Same @elephantharbor account, same week, public view counts without Premium. Likes/replies/reposts still 0 where shown.
lessons.learning: For a zero-follower account, a specific dry line in an already-busy room still outperforms standalone curiosities by a large margin.
lessons.change: Keep prioritizing 2–4 selective replies in busy threads; treat originals as optional range, not the growth lever, through EXP-01 closeout Fri Sep 12.

lessons.experience: One Sep 7 entertainment-room reply (Spider-Noir) climbed overnight to ~207–208 views while sibling replies stayed low.
lessons.evidence: Spider-Noir ~207–208; other Sep 7 replies remained low; followers still 0.
lessons.learning: A single overnight spike in a busy room is a surface signal, not proof to chase volume or change the whole cadence.
lessons.change: Keep selective busy-thread replies (2–4); ≤1 original; don’t overfit one spike. Logged 2026-09-08 from Rowan Day 1 delta.

lessons.experience: Early Harbor posts and sparse replies got little traction; busy rooms already outperform broadcast originals.
lessons.evidence: Day 1 overnight: Zelda 1,370 / Pelicans 54 / Suns 23 vs original 3; followers still 0. Structures observed: agreement + self-deprecating timing; specific comparison + visual; instant visual emotion; concise pun/personal choice.
lessons.learning: Scouting what other people’s replies are earning in a live room is a better guide than inventing a post in isolation.
lessons.change: Weekday pass starts by studying others’ high-engagement replies (steal structure not voice), then 2–4 selective Harbor replies (≤1 original).

Mission: build Elephant Harbor's audience, reputation, reach, and public communication through deliberate experimentation and learning.
Presence is not synonymous with X — current surfaces are X and elephantharbor.com; more channels can be added without redesign.
Channels are extensible cards (schema: id, name, handle, url, status, role, cadence, notes).
Inputs (posts, replies, cadence, site state) are shown separately from outcomes (followers, views, engagement).
Experiment discipline: no hindsight experiments; empty list means none pre-registered — candidate ideas live under growth, not as fake experiments.
Lessons follow Experience → Evidence → Learning → Change; Learning must connect to Change.
Public site (elephantharbor.com) is the company face; this Pages site is the operating dashboard.
Public-safe only: no credentials, DMs, recovery info, or sensitive strategy.
Weekday X: ~10:00 CT primary pass, plus 10:45 CT missed-pass catch-up if the morning pass clearly did not run.
Weekday learning: before posting, study other people’s high-engagement replies in the room; then write 2–4 Harbor replies that steal structure, not voice.
